title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This incident reveals a failure in mission planning for autonomous vehicles operating in known high-disruption conditions. Waymo deployed its fleet to San Francisco during Fourth of July celebrations without adequate safeguards against extended gridlock, which drained batteries faster than the vehicles could reach charging or pickup locations. The system was used outside the conditions it was designed for: extended immobility in stop-and-start traffic, combined with major road closures and crowd density that the company did not anticipate or prepare for.

The failure occurred at the point of deployment decision, not in the vehicle control systems themselves. A human evaluation of the traffic forecast and event schedule before the Fourth of July would have either reduced fleet size in high-risk areas, repositioned vehicles to avoid gridlock zones, or implemented battery reserve protocols. The company's roadside assistance had to retrieve the vehicles after the fact, treating the outcome as a crisis rather than a preventable operational mismatch.

It is not established whether Waymo's models or human operators failed to predict the traffic severity, or whether the prediction was made but the deployment proceeded anyway. A separate vehicle fire caused by fireworks shows a different vulnerability: the system's inability to detect and safely avoid hazards created by humans in the environment, though no injuries resulted from either incident.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday during Fourth of July celebrations when heavy traffic caused their batteries to drain. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on city streets following fireworks near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team towed the vehicles away, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during severe traffic events.

The incident created frustration among other motorists, with one driver spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic. A separate Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set off, though no injuries were reported. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss Saturday's traffic problems with public and private partners to improve future experiences. This is the second major traffic-related issue for Waymo in San Francisco, following a December incident where the company paused service during a widespread power outage.
